title: TACo: Training-Free, Hardware-Aware ViT Architecture Search with a Hypervolume-Based Unified Zero-Cost Score
evidence_span: TACo combines a zero-cost accuracy score with latency, energy, and activation memory in a hypervolume-based multi-objective search; CIFAR-10 and ImageNet-1K experiments reduce search from GPU-days to GPU-hours while finding balanced ViT architectures.
problem: Training each candidate makes hardware-aware ViT architecture search too expensive for multi-objective accuracy and deployment constraints.
method_or_artifact: Training-free zero-cost score and Pareto/hypervolume selection over accuracy, latency, energy, and activation memory.
workload_or_benchmark: CIFAR-10 and ImageNet-1K ViT architecture search; candidate space, hardware measurements, accuracy baselines, and search budgets are unspecified.
hardware_or_process_assumptions: Hardware-aware ViT deployment with latency, energy, and activation-memory estimates; target devices and measurement methodology are unspecified.
metrics: GPU-days to GPU-hours search reduction claimed
limits: The description omits absolute accuracy, search space, hardware calibration, energy boundary, and candidate count.
Training-free scores may mis-rank architectures under distribution or hardware changes.
Official description only; NAS claims require paper-level and deployment verification.

title: Thrend: Mitigating Counting Thread-Based Fine-Grained Timing on Arm and Apple CPUs
evidence_span: Thrend fuzzes counting threads, detects them with hardware-performance-counter sampling, and co-schedules suspected attackers and counting threads on one core; across four Arm and Apple devices at 100 Hz it reports 99.71% detection accuracy, 0% false negatives, and below 1.42% runtime overhead.
problem: Counting threads enable fine-grained timing side channels on Arm and Apple CPUs, while defenses must detect attacks without excessive runtime cost.
method_or_artifact: Fuzz-generated training corpus, performance-counter monitoring, and same-core co-scheduling defense.
workload_or_benchmark: Four Arm/Apple devices and timing-side-channel counting-thread workloads; processor models, OS versions, attack suite, and deployment policy are unspecified.
hardware_or_process_assumptions: Arm and Apple CPUs exposing hardware performance counters and scheduler controls; sampling access, privilege model, and core topology are unspecified.
metrics: Less than 1.42% runtime overhead at 100 Hz
limits: The description omits false-positive rate, workload impact, attack coverage, sampling energy, and device-specific variance.
Co-scheduling may reduce utilization or fail against adaptive attackers and unavailable counters.
Official description only; security claims require adversarial and deployment verification.

title: Slicemoe: Bit-Sliced Expert Caching Under Miss-Rate Constraints for Efficient MoE Inference
evidence_span: SliceMoE uses dynamic bit-sliced expert caching, calibration-free asymmetric Matryoshka quantization, and predictive cache warmup; on DeepSeek-V2-Lite and Qwen1.5-MoE-A2.7B it reports up to 2.37x/2.85x lower decode energy and 1.81x/1.64x lower decode latency while preserving near-high-bit accuracy.
problem: On-device MoE deployment is constrained by large expert parameters and expensive offloading, while prefetching or clustering can increase energy or reduce expert diversity.
method_or_artifact: Slice-level dynamic caching, mixed-precision truncation-compatible quantization, and prefill cache warmup under miss-rate constraints.
workload_or_benchmark: DeepSeek-V2-Lite and Qwen1.5-MoE-A2.7B decode inference; device, sequence/batch settings, accuracy thresholds, and baselines are unspecified.
hardware_or_process_assumptions: On-device MoE inference with limited memory and expert offloading; memory hierarchy, accelerator, bandwidth, and energy measurement boundary are unspecified.
metrics: Up to 2.37x and 2.85x lower decode energy
Up to 1.81x and 1.64x lower decode latency
limits: The description omits absolute accuracy, miss rates, memory capacity, model quantization, and end-to-end preprocessing costs.
Gains depend on expert popularity, sequence length, and hardware memory hierarchy.
Official description only; systems and quality claims require paper-level benchmark verification.

title: Phantom Walk: Reducing the Post-Migration Translation Path via Proactive Translation Dissemination in Multi-GPU Systems
evidence_span: Phantom Walk targets migration-induced translation misses in unified multi-GPU virtual memory by shortening post-migration page-fault and page-table-walk paths through proactive translation dissemination; evaluation reports 44.37% average overall performance improvement.
problem: Unified virtual memory page migrations invalidate GPU page-table entries and create migration-induced translation misses that degrade multi-GPU performance.
method_or_artifact: Proactive dissemination of translations to reduce post-migration GPU-local faults and page-table walks.
workload_or_benchmark: Multi-GPU unified-virtual-memory workloads; GPU model/count, migration policies, page sizes, application suite, and baselines are unspecified.
hardware_or_process_assumptions: Multi-GPU system with unified virtual memory and page migration; interconnect, TLB hierarchy, driver, and coherence assumptions are unspecified.
baselines: advanced page-migration policies without Phantom Walk
limits: The description omits translation-miss breakdown, memory overhead, migration traffic, application variance, and GPU configurations.
Proactive dissemination may increase metadata traffic or stale-state management cost.
Official description only; systems gains require trace and platform verification.

title: Towards Practical Live Migration for Heterogeneous Confidential Virtual Machines
evidence_span: The framework enables heterogeneous x86 CVM migration with a trusted migration agent that emulates required TEE-firmware migration commands; a prototype migrates between AMD SEV and Hygon CSV with comparable security guarantees to homogeneous migration and acceptable performance overhead.
problem: TEE-vendor-specific CVM implementations support migration mainly within homogeneous stacks, blocking cloud mobility across heterogeneous confidential hardware.
method_or_artifact: Generic heterogeneous-migration framework and trusted migration agent bridging AMD SEV and Hygon CSV command semantics.
workload_or_benchmark: Live migration between AMD SEV and Hygon CSV confidential VMs; VM workloads, downtime, bandwidth, threat model, and overhead values are unspecified.
hardware_or_process_assumptions: x86 confidential VMs, vendor TEE firmware, trusted migration agent, and cloud migration path; CPU generations, firmware versions, and attestation details are unspecified.
limits: The description omits downtime, bandwidth, cryptographic cost, failure behavior, and formal security equivalence.
Firmware emulation may expand the trusted computing base and depend on vendor-specific undocumented behavior.
Official description only; cloud security and performance claims require paper-level verification.

title: GTX: Graph Transformer for Parasitic Extraction on Analog Circuits
evidence_span: GTX combines customized parasitic modeling, hierarchical graph neural networks, and global attention for analog parasitic prediction; predicted-parasitics netlists closely match commercial PEX simulations, inference is 232.7x faster than commercial PEX, and simulation using predicted netlists is up to 8.4x faster.
problem: Commercial parasitic extraction and post-layout simulation are expensive, slowing layout-aware analog design iteration.
method_or_artifact: Graph-transformer parasitic surrogate capturing local device interactions and long-range interconnect dependencies.
workload_or_benchmark: Analog circuits and post-layout parasitic extraction compared with commercial PEX; process nodes, circuit suite, error metrics, and extraction configurations are unspecified.
hardware_or_process_assumptions: Analog layout-aware design with parasitic netlists and commercial extraction/simulation; PDK, geometry scale, and inference hardware are unspecified.
metrics: 232.7x faster parasitic inference than commercial PEX
Up to 8.4x faster simulation using predicted netlists
limits: The description omits absolute prediction error, failed circuits, PDK/process diversity, training cost, and hardware boundary.
Simulation agreement for selected circuits does not establish signoff-grade parasitic fidelity.
Official description only; analog EDA claims require paper-level and corner verification.

title: Instruction-Level Side-Channel Disassembly on Modern Complex CPUs via Voltage Waveform Analysis
evidence_span: The work constructs a dataset of 645 instructions including AVX/SSE and more than 50,000 voltage waveforms from a 3.1-GHz commercial x86 CPU under realistic multithreading, then uses CNN-Conformer encoding and Transformer decoding to reconstruct instruction sequences with 34.70% sequence accuracy, outperforming segmentation and classifier baselines.
problem: Out-of-order execution, deep pipelines, and noise make instruction recovery from power traces difficult on modern commercial CPUs.
method_or_artifact: End-to-end voltage-waveform sequence-to-sequence model with CNN-Conformer encoder and Transformer decoder.
workload_or_benchmark: 645 instructions and over 50,000 voltage samples on a 3.1-GHz x86 CPU under multithreading; trace setup, distance, sampling, and baseline values are unspecified.
hardware_or_process_assumptions: Commercial x86 processor with voltage side-channel observation and realistic multithreaded execution; board, sensor, access privilege, and countermeasures are unspecified.
limits: The description omits per-instruction accuracy, attacker access, noise robustness, cross-CPU transfer, and leakage mitigation.
Dataset and lab conditions may not represent remote or production attack settings.
Official description only; side-channel claims require responsible-disclosure and reproducibility review.

title: ISA-PM: A Unified ISA Extension and Microarchitecture Enabling Efficient ECPM in IoT Devices
evidence_span: ISA-PM supports ECPM across Montgomery and short-Weierstrass curves through a unified ISA and three-phase small-bit-width modular computation; AMD Virtex-7 FPGA experiments report up to 8.37x area-time-product improvement over state-of-the-art lightweight ECPM accelerators.
problem: Curve-specific ECPM accelerators do not scale across field parameters and force redesigns for multi-curve IoT cryptography.
method_or_artifact: Unified ISA extension and microarchitecture with bit-width decomposition and design-space exploration over resource parallelism.
workload_or_benchmark: ECPM for multiple elliptic curves on AMD Virtex-7 FPGA; curve set, frequency, resource use, security checks, and baseline implementations are unspecified.
hardware_or_process_assumptions: Area-constrained IoT cryptographic accelerator with flexible modular arithmetic; FPGA implementation and ISA integration details are unspecified.
metrics: Up to 8.37x area-time-product improvement on AMD Virtex-7
limits: The description omits absolute area, latency, energy, frequency, curve coverage, and software overhead.
Flexibility may trade peak performance against dedicated curve accelerators.
Official description only; cryptographic hardware claims require paper-level verification.

title: EPAR: Electromagnetic Pathways to Architectural Reliability in Quantum Processors
evidence_span: EPAR maps electromagnetic layout distortion to effective Hamiltonians, mediated connectivity, and control-pulse response; across tested layouts its structural scores agree 100% with two-qubit error trends and reveal over 10x robustness differences among edges with identical calibrated error rates.
problem: Conventional calibrated error rates do not expose how physical electromagnetic layout choices affect execution-level reliability in scaling superconducting processors.
method_or_artifact: Electromagnetic-to-architecture framework reconstructing Hamiltonian perturbations and compiler-relevant robustness scores early from physical design.
workload_or_benchmark: Superconducting quantum processor layouts and two-qubit error trends; layout count, calibration protocol, electromagnetic solver, and compiler tasks are unspecified.
hardware_or_process_assumptions: Superconducting qubits, electromagnetic coupling, control pulses, and physical layouts; process, frequency, packaging, and noise assumptions are unspecified.
metrics: 100% agreement with two-qubit error trends across tested layouts
Over 10x robustness differences among edges with identical calibrated error rates
limits: The description omits absolute error rates, layout/sample count, calibration drift, solver cost, and experimental validation.
Structural agreement in tested layouts does not establish predictive generalization across devices or packaging.
Official description only; quantum reliability claims require paper-level and hardware validation.

title: Autonomous Evolution of EDA Tools: Multi-Agent Self-Evolved ABC
evidence_span: The framework uses multiple LLM agents to propose and implement ABC source changes, validates correctness, and evaluates QoR on standard benchmark circuits, iteratively discovering synthesis improvements beyond seeded human heuristics and external research code.
problem: Logic-synthesis heuristics plateau, while manual improvement of a complex monolithic EDA codebase is slow and difficult to scale.
method_or_artifact: Multi-agent LLM code-evolution loop with correctness validation and benchmark QoR feedback over the ABC repository.
workload_or_benchmark: ABC logic-synthesis codebase and standard benchmark circuits; QoR metrics, number of iterations, code changes, model versions, and baseline tool results are unspecified.
hardware_or_process_assumptions: EDA software repository with synthesis correctness tests and benchmark-based QoR evaluation; target libraries, compute budget, and human review are unspecified.
metrics: QoR improvements beyond seeded heuristics claimed qualitatively
limits: The description omits numeric QoR, regression rate, search cost, code-review burden, and reproducibility details.
Autonomous code changes may overfit benchmark circuits or introduce latent correctness and maintainability risks.
Official description only; software-evolution claims require artifact and independent benchmark review.
